newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Australia sells grounded Nomad planes to Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Australia sells grounded Nomad planes to Indonesia.

text.p: Australia announced on Thursday it is selling its grounded fleet of 20 Nomad aircraft to Indonesia.
The Australian Defence Force grounded the Nomads in November 1994 after army pilots refused to fly the Australian-designed and built aircraft following a number of fatal accidents.

Australian Defence Minister Ian McLachlan said in a statement the sale was subject to final price negotiations and a final inspection of the aircraft, which are currently in storage at the Army Aviation Centre in Oakey, Queensland.
"Indonesia is interested in the aircraft for maritime surveillance, a role in which it already uses 18 Nomad aircraft acquired from Australia in the 1970s," McLachlan said.

"Maritime surveillance is well within the approved performance limitations on Nomad aircraft and in contrast to the demanding role the aircraft had in the ADF as general support aircraft for the army," he said in Surabaya, East Java.
McLachlan and Indonesian Defence Minister Edi Sudradjat met in Surabaya for the second annual talks between the defence ministers of the two countries.

An Australian parliamentary inquiry in May found failure to follow inspection and maintenance procedures in 1990 caused a Royal Australian Air Force Nomad to crash during training exercises near Adelaide.
Investigators found the twin-prop plane's tail had fallen off. Worldwide, 19 of the 170 Nomads ever built have crashed, killing 56 people.
An army report in July 1995 recommended the aircraft be scrapped because the restrictions necessary for safe flying made them too expensive and ineffective for Australian military use.
